mechanics.mechanic: Open by defining the subject, explaining why it matters to a broad audience, and previewing the distinctive angle the discussion will take.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of an educational piece to establish relevance and create expectations about what will be covered.
mechanics.avoid: Do not overpromise novelty or imply that the featured angle replaces more established fundamentals.

mechanics.mechanic: Distinguish the main topic from adjacent topics, briefly acknowledge related material, and state which areas will receive only limited treatment.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the subject is broad, controversial, or connected to several bodies of knowledge.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce so many side topics that the central argument becomes unclear.

mechanics.function: Establish a governing principle before adding nuance
mechanics.mechanic: Present the simplest widely accepted rule first, then explain how context, mechanisms, or individual variation complicate its application.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when introducing a specialized framework that could otherwise seem to contradict common understanding.
mechanics.avoid: Do not dismiss the foundational rule merely to make the new perspective appear more radical.

mechanics.function: Translate technical mechanisms into a small number of stages
mechanics.mechanic: Reduce a complex process into a memorable sequence of functional steps, define each step in plain language, and repeatedly connect later interventions to the relevant step.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for scientific, technical, or procedural explanations where many details could overwhelm the audience.
mechanics.avoid: Do not confuse a simplified teaching model with a complete account of the underlying process.

mechanics.mechanic: Start with an intuitive metaphor or everyday description, add only the terminology needed for precision, and explicitly signal when deeper technical detail is optional.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when addressing mixed audiences with different levels of expertise.
mechanics.avoid: Do not let metaphors replace causal explanation or introduce misleading equivalences.

mechanics.mechanic: Separate established principles, plausible mechanisms, preliminary findings, and practical suggestions; acknowledge uncertainty without abandoning the actionable implication.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use whenever evidence quality varies or a proposed application extends beyond direct research findings.
mechanics.avoid: Do not present correlational observations, laboratory mechanisms, and proven interventions as equivalent forms of evidence.

mechanics.mechanic: Anticipate the strongest reasonable objection, state why it may matter, and explain how the main interpretation remains viable or should be narrowed.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use after presenting a surprising result or counterintuitive claim.
mechanics.avoid: Do not invent weak objections merely to dismiss them, and do not bury important limitations after the recommendation.

mechanics.function: Convert mechanisms into practical leverage points
mechanics.mechanic: After explaining the causal pathway, identify the controllable inputs that could influence it and distinguish primary options from supplementary ones.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use in applied educational content where the audience needs to move from understanding to action.
mechanics.avoid: Do not imply that manipulating one pathway guarantees a particular outcome or overrides broader constraints.

mechanics.mechanic: Periodically restate the central sequence or principle, then use it as a bridge into the next example, intervention, or implication.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use in long-form explanations with multiple sections or accumulating technical concepts.
mechanics.avoid: Do not repeat the same summary without advancing the argument or adding a new application.
